name: Cholpon-Ata Rock Gallery
near: Cholpon-Ata: ≈3 km from the town center, in the foothills above the airfield (runway); up to an hour on foot from the center.
elev: ≈1700–1750 m (estimate: Cholpon-Ata by the lake is ≈1620 m, the petroglyph field is on a gentle foothill slope above the town; the exact elevation of the entrance is not published in the sources)
short: A field of boulders of ≈42 ha on the slope above Cholpon-Ata with hundreds of petroglyphs from the Bronze Age to the Middle Ages (2nd millennium BC to the 4th century AD and later): ibexes, deer, snow leopards, hunting scenes. Three marked routes from 800 m to 3 km.
desc: The open-air petroglyph museum occupies about 42 hectares of stony foothills between the Kungey Ala-Too range and the lake. Thousands of boulders brought by a glacier are carved with images of mountain ibexes (the majority: in one sample of 409 petroglyphs there were 285 ibexes), deer, camels, snow leopards, and scenes of hunting, battles and festivals. The oldest date to the 1st–2nd millennium BC (Saka-Wusun period), some to the Turkic era and the Middle Ages; the site has no single date. Besides the drawings, the area has stone circles, burial mounds, balbals and remains of walls. Three routes have been laid out: 800 m (30–40 min, with blue markers — the best developed), 1.5 km (≈1.5 h) and 3 km (≈2 h); at the entrance is the main stone with the most striking drawings. There are signs in three languages, but few; you have to look for some of the petroglyphs yourself. There is no shade or water on the site, and cattle roam the field. A UNESCO nomination was being prepared; the site is not on the list. From the upper part of the field there is a panorama of Issyk-Kul and Terskey Ala-Too.
guide: Start with the big stone by the ticket window — it has the clearest snow leopards and ibexes — and then follow the blue flags of the short loop: in 40 minutes you will see the main things, and the rest of the field is for those who like hunting for drawings like treasure. Look at the boulders from the south, sun-baked side: the ancient masters chose the dark “desert varnish”, on which light lines show best, which is why the drawings often face the lake. Come in the morning or toward evening — slanting light pulls shadows out of the carved lines, while at noon the petroglyphs “disappear”. You can pay the caretaker for a tour: without the story the field looks like a scatter of stones, with it — like a gallery. Don't step on the stones with drawings and don't trace them — they are protected by nothing but your care.
see: The main stone at the entrance with snow leopards and ibexes; petroglyphs with hunting scenes, deer, camels; stone circles and burial mounds, balbals; a panorama of Issyk-Kul from the upper part of the field; routes of 800 m / 1.5 km / 3 km.
skip: If you expect a museum with display cases and air conditioning — this is a bare field of stones with no shade. If you have already seen Saimaluu-Tash or Cholpon-Ata — it is not the main interest: there are not many drawings relative to the area, and many people don't find them without a guide. If the heat is above 30° and you have no hat — better to postpone until evening.
diff: Easy: a walk on an uneven stony slope, routes of 0.8–3 km, small ascent. Closed shoes are needed.
when: April to October; in summer only in the morning/evening because of the heat with no shade; accessible in winter, but the stones are slippery after snow/rain. Crowds peak in July–August and on the days of the Nomad Games.
hours: Google Maps (03.10.2026): daily 08:00–20:00; 2GIS: daily with no days off; eurasia.travel: from 8:00. In practice — daylight hours; out of season the ticket booth may be closed, the field is open.
daytime: Early morning or 2 hours before sunset — slanting light brings out the lines of the petroglyphs, and there is no heat. Midday is the worst time (flat light, scorching).
how: From Bishkek: marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek → Cholpon-Ata from the Bishkek bus station (Alma-Atinskaya St. 1/1; the Western station has been closed since 10.2024), 400–450 som, ≈3–3.5 h (24.kg, 2024); GoBus 580 som (2024); a taxi 700–1000 som/person. In Cholpon-Ata: from the center 3 km north, toward the airfield — by taxi (Yandex Go/local) or on foot up to 1 h; there are no signs, ask for directions. There is parking at the entrance.
needcar: No: from the center of Cholpon-Ata you can walk (3 km, up to an hour) or take a taxi in a few minutes. You only need a car if you are not in Cholpon-Ata.
self: Yes, fully: the short route is marked with blue signs; to “read” the drawings, a guide or the I Love KG description is useful.
roadtype: Paved road through the town to the outskirts, the last few hundred meters are dirt/gravel to the parking area (I Love KG); inside — trails on a stony slope, uneven ground.
traveltime: From the center of Cholpon-Ata 5–10 min by taxi, 40–60 min on foot; from Bishkek ≈3.5–4 h. A visit takes: 30–40 min (short loop) to 2–3 h (full), up to midday per reviews.
stay: In Cholpon-Ata: private rooms 600–1500 som/night, guesthouses up to 3000 som at peak (July–August), mid-range hotels $15–20/person, premium resorts $184–528/night (24.kg, 2024). Names: Ak Bermet, Karven Four Seasons, Tri Korony (Three Crowns), Akun, Goluboy Issyk-Kul (Blue Issyk-Kul) (weproject 2024).
net: Cholpon-Ata is a town, with Beeline/O!/MegaCom 4G coverage; in April 2026 Beeline strengthened its network in Cholpon-Ata (economist.kg). On the field itself, 3 km from the center, a signal is expected, but there are no separate measurements.
entry: According to Yandex Maps reviews (2024–2026): 80 som, in some reviews 100 som per person; 2GIS — “entry is paid”; in 2015 — 40–50 som (ZigZag on Earth). The caretaker's tour is separate, by arrangement. The museum's official rate is not published.
transfer: A taxi within Cholpon-Ata to the museum — roughly 100–200 som (estimated from city rates, not confirmed by a price list); marshrutka (minibus) from Bishkek 400–450 som, GoBus 580 (2024). Sightseeing excursions with a stop here — see Tripster/Sputnik8, prices on request.
bring: Water, a hat, sunscreen, closed shoes for uneven stones, cash in som (ticket booth and guide), a camera with a zoom — the drawings are small.
warn: There is no shade or water — scorching in summer. The petroglyphs are protected by nothing: don't step on the stones, trace or “refresh” the lines. Cattle roam the field — watch your step. There is construction nearby, and some signs are damaged (reviews 2025–2026). The ticket booth is partly informal: ask for a receipt.
food: There is nothing on site. In Cholpon-Ata there are cafes and canteens: a canteen from ≈1000 som for three meals, an average bill in a cafe of ≈1400 som for a snack, 2700 for dinner (24.kg 2024); local fish (chebak, farmed trout), lagman, samsa, ashlan-fu.
reviews: Google Maps: 4.2/5, 886 ratings (03.10.2026). Yandex Maps: 4.6/5, 104 reviews, 81% positive (07.10.2026). 2GIS: 4.7/5, 23 ratings (07.10.2026). Pros: views of the lake and mountains, the antiquity, the large area, a friendly caretaker, souvenirs. Cons: few signs and little information, “lots of stones — few drawings”, heat, cattle and dirt, construction nearby, poor upkeep.
p.sum: The site is within the town limits of Cholpon-Ata: from the center 20–40 minutes on foot uphill (north, toward the airfield) or 5–10 minutes by taxi/Yandex Go; there is parking at the entrance. To Cholpon-Ata itself from Bishkek — a marshrutka (minibus) from the Bishkek bus station (Alma-Atinskaya St. 1/1, 400–600 som, 3.5–5 h) or the summer train to Balykchy + a marshrutka (minibus). Come early in the morning or 2 hours before sunset, take water and a hat; it is convenient to combine with Rukh Ordo in one day.

p.iti.2.title: What to combine it with
p.iti.2.plan: Rukh Ordo (3.2 km), the Nomad Games hippodrome, the Chon-Ak-Suu gorge (≈35 km east) and Semyonovka (≈40 km), Bosteri.
p.season: April to October; July–August — scorching by day and crowds (visit in the morning/evening), on the days of the Nomad Games — a rush; in winter the field is accessible, but the stones are under snow/ice and the ticket booth may not work. The ticket booth is open ≈08:00–20:00 in season.
p.budget.economy: ≈2500–4000 som/day: marshrutka (minibus) from Bishkek 500 (or train 150–180 + a marshrutka (minibus) to Cholpon-Ata), entry 80–100, guesthouse 1500–3000 (per room), canteen 1000
p.permits: Not needed. Entry is paid at the ticket booth: 80–100 som/person according to 2024–2026 reviews (the official rate is not published); the caretaker's tour is separate.
p.access: With children — yes (the short 800 m loop); for older people — the short route, uneven stones; with a stroller — effectively no (dirt and stones); with a dog — allowed, on a leash (cattle).
